messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Confirmed the working tree is clean; no repository changes have been made.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and adjust feature placement, paths, and world-population density.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test exploration, movement, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Update region sizes and coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test exploration, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes and coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`.
- Region sizes currently range from 34–38 tiles; water features use fixed coordinates, material nodes are fixed at 8, and normal enemies at 15 per region.
- `buildWorld()` currently adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, in addition to region-defined NPCs.
- `returnToHub()` uses the current region except for dungeon returns; death respawn behavior also needs review.
- Dungeon return UI describes a 500g fee.
- Offline market buyer simulation is distinct from multiplayer; no multiplayer server exists.

Do not edit files. Be thorough but focused on camera, rendering, minimap, collision, and mobile constraints.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e49f67103ffe92jvHcZeu2ElFB" state="completed">
## 64-tile map assessment

**A 64×64 world appears compatible with the existing size-based bounds, but it raises map-wide setup and minimap costs, while leaving much of the configured content clustered near its current coordinates.** The most noticeable scaling is likely when a world is created or its minimap is redrawn—not from drawing every ground tile on every frame.

### Performance implications

- **World generation and ground prerender scale with tile count.** The generator allocates `size * size` tiles and initializes them in nested loops; the renderer likewise visits every tile to build a single ground canvas. A 64×64 map has **4,096 tiles**: about **3.16×** a 36×36 map and **2.84×** a 38×38 map.  
  References: [world.js:205–229](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js#L205), [renderer.js:62–71](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js#L62), [renderer.js:132–153](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js#L132).

- **The ground canvas also gets substantially larger.** Its dimensions are based on map size, with a 192-pixel margin in each dimension; tile dimensions are 64×32 pixels. Including that margin, a 64-tile canvas has about **2.86× the pixel area** of a 36-tile canvas. The canvas is constructed when the world is set, and the renderer draws that prerendered bitmap during normal rendering.  
  References: [renderer.js:7–10, 62–69](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js#L7), [renderer.js:132–153](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js#L132), [renderer.js:521–529](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js#L521).

- **Minimap redraws repeat full-map work.** Each redraw iterates through all `size²` tiles. There are two redraw paths: the renderer redraws at intervals over 220 ms, and HUD updates call `updateMinimap()`; the game emits HUD updates at 0.1-second intervals. These paths can both contribute work, although the actual combined redraw rate depends on how the updates overlap.  
  References: [renderer.js:620–625, 1266–1289](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js#L620), [game.js:144–152](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js#L144), [ui.js:447–453](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js#L447).

- **Visible-object filtering still scans object lists.** Each render checks props, nodes, hidden objects, NPCs, enemies, and loot before filtering by visibility. That cost depends on object counts, not directly on tile area. Open-world enemies are currently fixed at 15 normal enemies plus a boss, so enemy iteration does not automatically grow with a larger map.  
  References: [renderer.js:538–577](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js#L538), [world.js:434–446](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js#L434).

### Compatibility and content-placement risks

- **Core movement and camera bounds are size-relative.** Camera clamping uses generated ground dimensions; collision, tile lookup, and player boundary clamping use `world.size`. These are positive signs that increasing map size alone does not violate an obvious fixed map-bound assumption in those paths.  
  References: [renderer.js:119–126](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js#L119), [world.js:58–63, 340–355](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js#L58), [game.js:225–232](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js#L225).

- **Configured landmarks remain in their old coordinate ranges.** Current region sizes are 34, 36, or 38 tiles, with spawn, village, and lair coordinates generally around 16–31. If those regions are enlarged without relocating landmarks, the map grows around content that remains concentrated in the existing portion. Pond coordinates are also configured explicitly rather than derived from map size.  
  References: [data.js:162–249](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js#L162), [world.js:232–249](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js#L232).

- **Several content counts will not fill the added area proportionally.** Random scenery count is `floor(size * 2.4)`: that rises from 86 props at size 36 to 153 at size 64—about **1.78×**, versus **3.16×** as many tiles. Resource nodes are fixed at eight, and open-world enemies remain fixed at 16 including the boss. Unless counts or placement rules change, a larger world is likely to feel less densely populated.  
  References: [world.js:175–191, 284–306](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js#L175), [world.js:434–446](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js#L434).

**Bottom line:** The inspected bounds and coordinate handling are predominantly size-driven, so 64 tiles look mechanically plausible. The clearest risks are the roughly threefold increase in map-wide tile work, repeated full-map minimap redraws, and content density/landmark placement that does not expand with the world.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; a 64-tile map was assessed as plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Assessed 64-tile map scaling: size-relative bounds appear compatible; tile generation/rendering/minimap work increases roughly threefold, and landmark/content density needs adjustment.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Optimize/review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds and mobile.
- Test exploration, movement, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Reduce or bound repeated full-map minimap work in `src/renderer.js` if needed.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes and coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`.
- Region sizes currently range from 34–38 tiles; water features use fixed coordinates, material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- `buildWorld()` currently adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, in addition to region-defined NPCs.
- `returnToHub()` returns to the current region except for dungeon returns; death respawn also returns to the current region.
- Dungeon return UI describes a 500g fee.
- Offline market buyer simulation is distinct from multiplayer; no multiplayer server exists.

## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; a 64-tile map was assessed as plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Assessed 64-tile map scaling: size-relative bounds appear compatible; tile generation/rendering/minimap work increases roughly threefold, and landmark/content density needs adjustment.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Optimize/review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds and mobile.
- Test exploration, movement, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Reduce or bound repeated full-map minimap work in `src/renderer.js` if needed.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes and coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`.
- Region sizes currently range from 34–38 tiles; water features use fixed coordinates, material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- `buildWorld()` currently adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, in addition to region-defined NPCs.
- `returnToHub()` returns to the current region except for dungeon returns; death respawn also returns to the current region.
- Dungeon return UI describes a 500g fee.
- Offline market buyer simulation is distinct from multiplayer; no multiplayer server exists.
- A 64×64 map appears compatible with size-based bounds, but would increase tile setup and minimap work to roughly three times the current scale; configured landmarks/content would need repositioning.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; a 64-tile map was assessed as plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Assessed 64×64 map scaling: size-relative bounds appear compatible; tile generation/rendering/minimap work increases roughly threefold, and landmarks/content density need adjustment.
- Confirmed later-region NPC definitions currently include quest keepers and teleporters; `buildWorld()` also adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region.
- Confirmed `returnToHub()` and death respawn currently return players to their current region; the dungeon return UI describes a 500g fee.
- Confirmed the minimap redraws periodically (every 220ms) and traverses the world tiles.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Optimize/review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds and mobile.
- Test exploration, movement, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Reduce or bound repeated full-map minimap work in `src/renderer.js` if needed.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes and coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`.
- Region sizes currently range from 34–38 tiles; water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- No changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; a 64×64 map was assessed as plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Assessed 64×64 map scaling: size-relative bounds appear compatible; tile generation/rendering/minimap work increases roughly threefold, and landmarks/content density need adjustment.
- Confirmed later-region NPC definitions include quest keepers and teleporters; `buildWorld()` also adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region.
- Confirmed `returnToHub()` and death respawn currently return players to their current region; the dungeon return UI describes a 500g fee.
- Confirmed the minimap redraws periodically (every 220ms) and traverses the world tiles.
- No repository files have been changed.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Optimize/review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds and mobile.
- Test exploration, movement, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Reduce or bound repeated full-map minimap work in `src/renderer.js` if needed.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes and coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`.
- Region sizes currently range from 34–38 tiles; water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- `returnToHub()` charges 500g in dungeons and returns to the current region; death respawn also returns to the current region.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; a 64×64 map was assessed as plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Assessed 64×64 map scaling: size-relative bounds appear compatible; tile generation/rendering/minimap work increases roughly threefold, and landmarks/content density need adjustment.
- Confirmed later-region NPC definitions include quest keepers and teleporters; `buildWorld()` also adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region.
- Confirmed `returnToHub()` and death respawn currently return players to their current region; the dungeon return UI describes a 500g fee.
- Confirmed the minimap redraws periodically (every 220ms) and traverses the world tiles.
- No repository files have been changed.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Optimize/review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds and mobile.
- Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Reduce or bound repeated full-map minimap work in `src/renderer.js` if needed.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes and coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`.
- Region sizes currently range from 34–38 tiles; water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- `returnToHub()` charges 500g in dungeons and returns to the current region; death respawn also returns to the current region.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; 64×64 maps were assessed as plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Assessed that increasing maps to 64×64 roughly triples tile/rendering/minimap work; existing world-bound checks are size-relative, but landmarks and content density need adjustment.
- Confirmed `buildWorld()` adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region; teleporter NPCs are already defined in all regions.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Optimize/review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds and mobile.
- Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes/coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`; current region sizes are 34–38 tiles.
- Water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- `returnToHub()` currently returns to the current region and charges 500g in dungeons; death respawn also returns to the current region.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; 64×64 maps were assessed as plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Assessed that increasing maps to 64×64 roughly triples tile/rendering/minimap work; world-bound checks are size-relative, but landmarks and content density need adjustment.
- Confirmed `buildWorld()` adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region; teleporter NPCs and quest keepers are already defined across regions.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Optimize/review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds and mobile.
- Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes/coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`; current sizes are 34–38 tiles.
- Water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- `returnToHub()` currently returns to the current region and charges 500g in dungeons; death respawn also returns to the current region.
- The latest inspection found no code changes or implementation decisions.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; 64×64 maps were considered plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Confirmed `buildWorld()` adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region; quest keepers and teleporters are configured across regions.
- Confirmed the repository was clean at the latest status check; no code changes have been made.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes/coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`; current sizes are 34–38 tiles.
- Water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- `returnToHub()` currently returns to the current region and charges 500g in dungeons; death respawn also returns to the current region.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; 64×64 maps were considered plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Confirmed `buildWorld()` adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region; quest keepers and teleporters are configured across regions.
- Confirmed the repository was clean at the latest status check; no code changes have been made.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes/coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`; current sizes are 34–38 tiles.
- Water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- `returnToHub()` currently returns to the current region and charges 500g in dungeons; death respawn also returns to the current region.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; 64×64 maps were considered plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Confirmed `buildWorld()` adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region; quest keepers and teleporters are configured across regions.
- No code changes have been made; the initial shell check found no `package.json`.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes/coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`; current sizes are 34–38 tiles.
- Water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- `returnToHub()` currently returns to the current region and charges 500g in dungeons; death respawn also returns to the current region.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand every AETHERIA region into a larger, more varied exploration map while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Prepare the game for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players, while keeping it playable and optimized for mobile.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions yet; 64×64 maps were considered plausible but not selected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region configuration, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Confirmed there is no multiplayer server; offline market buyers are simulated for offline play.
- Confirmed `buildWorld()` adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region; quest keepers and teleporters are configured across regions.
- Confirmed the renderer pre-renders all ground tiles and updates the minimap periodically; these costs scale with map size.
- No code changes have been made.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; retain later-region quest keepers and make later-region teleporters return to Greendale.
- Update `returnToHub()` and death respawn behavior for later regions and dungeons.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes/coordinates, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, and world population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, `returnToHub()`, and death respawn.
- `src/ui.js`: NPC dialogue, role actions, travel UI, and dungeon return action.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.
- `src/state.js`: Save and progress persistence.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`; sizes currently range from 34–38 tiles.
- Water features use fixed coordinates; material nodes are fixed at 8, normal enemies at 15 per region, and scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Village structures, clearings, paths, and lair placement use fixed tile offsets that must be checked when resizing.
- Player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`; `enterRegion()` uses them on startup.
- `returnToHub()` currently returns to the current region and charges 500g in dungeons; death respawn also returns to the current region.
- The world-map travel UI currently allows region travel; later-region teleporter destination restrictions still need implementation.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e49eed2f0ffe7t5aUEOaDewzVF" state="completed" description="Inspect world expansion code">
## Findings

**Current dimensions:** all eight regions are configured at sizes 34, 36, or 38. Each region’s spawn, village, and lair are explicit coordinates in [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js:162-253`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js ).

### Coordinate assumptions to review

- **Configured landmarks remain at fixed coordinates.** Spawn, village, and lair coordinates are listed per region in `data.js`. Increasing `size` alone won’t move them toward the new center or edges; they’ll stay where they are. That may be intentional, but it affects landmark spacing and how much of a larger map those landmarks occupy.
- **Ponds are also fixed per region.** Their centers and radii are hard-coded in [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js:232-249`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js ). The water placement checks bounds, so it avoids out-of-range tile writes, but larger regions won’t reposition or scale these features.
- **Paths mix fixed and size-derived endpoints.** The spawn-to-village and village-to-lair paths use landmark coordinates; other paths start from fixed offsets such as `4` and `vy - 3`, then run toward `size - 4` ([`world.js:251-256`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js)). These remain in-bounds, but may not provide suitable routes or coverage as layouts change.
- **Village and lair layouts use fixed offsets and radii.** The village plaza, houses, and furnishings are positioned relative to the village using fixed values ([`world.js:133-173`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js)). They are not dimension-scaled; treat that as a deliberate fixed-size landmark footprint unless the design calls for larger landmarks.
- **Some generated content counts don’t scale with map area.** Resource nodes stay at 8, normal enemies at 15, and roadside details at 18, while the general prop budget scales with size ([`world.js:175-190`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js), [`world.js:284-306`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js), [`world.js:421-446`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js)). Expanding maps could therefore make these elements less dense.
- **Safe-spawn recovery has a fixed search radius.** `findSafeSpawn` searches up to radius 14, then falls back to a position relative to the village without checking it again ([`world.js:321-334`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js)). This is worth covering with spawn-safety checks when changing landmark placement or obstruction patterns.

### What already adapts to map size

Tile allocation and generation bounds, node and scenery placement ranges, hidden-chest edge positions, movement and collision bounds, and the renderer’s world dimensions all use the configured size. Relevant code includes [`world.js:205-229`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js), [`world.js:175-203`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js), [`game.js:225-232`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js), and [`renderer.js:62-71`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/renderer.js).

### Region-count assumptions

If “expanding all regions” means adding regions as well as enlarging maps, the profile’s visited-region display has a hard-coded `/8` in [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js:854-859`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js). It also derives the numerator from only the starting region and current region, not a history of all regions visited. Another literal “8 regions” appears in the About panel at [`ui.js:1254-1260`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js). By contrast, the game’s region progress total derives from `REGION_ORDER.length` ([`game.js:1033-1037`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js)).

## Validation and implementation plan

I found no map-specific tests or root `package.json`/test runner. The GitHub workflow at [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.github/workflows/opencode.yml`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.github/workflows/opencode.yml ) is issue-triggered OpenCode automation, not an apparent project build/test workflow. The startup scripts invoke runtime-provided scripts: [`start.sh`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh ) calls `default-start.mjs`, [`capture.sh`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh ) calls `default-capture.mjs`, and [`startup.sh`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/startup.sh ) only sets strict shell options.

A safe implementation plan would be to centralize or derive each region’s landmark and water layout, then validate invariants for every region: landmark and pond bounds, viable paths, unobstructed player spawns, and intended content density. Add map-generation checks before changing layouts, and separately make the profile’s region count and visited tracking consistent with the region data.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand all AETHERIA regions for more varied exploration while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Keep the game playable and optimized for mobile, and prepare for future 200–300-player multiplayer without fake players.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning players to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- No map dimensions or expansion approach selected yet.
- Later-region leyline travel is being restricted to Greendale; returning from later regions and dying there now sends the player to Greendale.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected region layouts, world generation, NPCs, quest access, travel/respawn, rendering, minimap, and online-status messaging.
- Updated `Game.travelTo()` in `src/game.js` to reject travel from regions after Ironcrag unless the destination is Greendale.
- Updated `returnToHub()` and death respawn in `src/game.js` to return players from later regions to Greendale.
- Updated `panelMap()` in `src/ui.js` to show only Greendale as the travel destination from later regions and hide dungeon listings there.
- Confirmed no map-specific tests or root package/test runner were found.

### Active
- Expand region sizes and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for varied exploration.
- Keep services on Greendale and Ironcrag; remove the extra provisioner and field smith from later regions while retaining their quest keepers and Greendale-return teleporters.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes, landmarks, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, resource nodes, and enemy population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, return behavior, death respawn, and saved coordinates.
- `src/ui.js`: World-map travel UI and NPC services.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.

## Important Context
- `REGION_ORDER`: `greendale`, `ironcrag`, `venomwood`, `mistgrave`, `frostpeak`, `sunscorch`, `ashen`, `tower`; sizes currently range from 34–38 tiles.
- `buildWorld()` still adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region; this conflicts with the service-location requirement.
- Quest keepers and teleporters are configured across regions in `src/data.js`.
- Water features use fixed coordinates; nodes remain at 8 and roadside details at 18, while normal enemies remain at 15 per region; scenery count scales as `size * 2.4`.
- Village structures, paths, clearings, and lair placement use fixed tile offsets that need review when resizing.
- Saved player region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`.
- Renderer pre-renders all ground tiles and updates the minimap periodically; these costs increase with map size.
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests or runtime verification have been performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand all AETHERIA regions for more varied exploration while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Keep the game mobile-playable and optimized, with future multiplayer capacity in mind and no fake players.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- From regions after Ironcrag, leyline travel is restricted to Greendale.
- Returning from later regions and dying there sends the player to Greendale.
- No map dimensions or expansion approach selected yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Game.travelTo()` rejects travel from regions after Ironcrag to destinations other than Greendale.
- `returnToHub()` and death respawn send players in later regions to Greendale.
- `panelMap()` shows only Greendale as the travel destination from later regions and hides dungeon listings there.

### Active
- Expand region dimensions and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content for exploration.
- Remove Camp Provisioner and Field Smith from regions after Ironcrag while retaining quest keepers and Greendale-return teleporters.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes, landmarks, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, resource nodes, and enemy population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, return behavior, death respawn, and saved coordinates.
- `src/ui.js`: World-map travel UI and NPC services.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.

## Important Context
- Region sizes are currently 34–38 tiles; `REGION_ORDER` has eight regions.
- `buildWorld()` still adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, conflicting with the service-location requirement.
- Landmark coordinates and ponds are fixed; village and lair layouts use fixed offsets.
- Resource nodes remain at 8, normal enemies at 15, and roadside details at 18, while scenery scales with map size.
- Renderer pre-renders all ground tiles; minimap updates periodically. Both costs grow with map size.
- Saved region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`.
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests or runtime verification have been performed. No map-specific tests or root package/test runner were found.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand all AETHERIA regions for more varied exploration while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Keep the game mobile-playable and optimized, with future multiplayer capacity and no fake players.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- From regions after Ironcrag, leyline travel is restricted to Greendale.
- Returning from later regions and dying there sends the player to Greendale.
- No map dimensions or expansion approach selected yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Game.travelTo()` rejects travel from regions after Ironcrag to destinations other than Greendale.
- `returnToHub()` and death respawn send players in later regions to Greendale.
- `panelMap()` shows only Greendale as the travel destination from later regions and hides dungeon listings there.

### Active
- Expand region dimensions and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content.
- Remove Camp Provisioner and Field Smith from regions after Ironcrag while retaining quest keepers and Greendale-return teleporters.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose larger map dimensions and update region sizes and landmark coordinates in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes, landmarks, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, resource nodes, and enemy population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, return behavior, death respawn, and saved coordinates.
- `src/ui.js`: World-map travel UI, NPC services, and region progress display.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `src/game.js` and `src/ui.js` were already modified before the latest inspection. Preserve and inspect those changes before editing.
- Region sizes are currently 34–38 tiles across eight regions in `REGION_ORDER`.
- `buildWorld()` still adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, conflicting with the service-location requirement.
- Landmark coordinates, ponds, and village/lair layouts use fixed offsets; resource nodes remain at 8, normal enemies at 15, and roadside details at 18.
- Renderer pre-renders all ground tiles; minimap updates periodically. Both costs grow with map size.
- Saved region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`.
- No root `package.json` was found; no tests or runtime verification have been performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand all AETHERIA regions for more varied exploration while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Keep the game mobile-playable and optimized, with future multiplayer capacity and no fake players.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- From regions after Ironcrag, leyline travel is restricted to Greendale.
- Returning from later regions and dying there sends the player to Greendale.
- Greendale’s map expansion was started at size 56, with spawn, village, and lair repositioned proportionally; other map dimensions remain undecided.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Game.travelTo()` rejects travel from regions after Ironcrag to destinations other than Greendale.
- `returnToHub()` and death respawn send players in later regions to Greendale.
- `panelMap()` shows only Greendale as the travel destination from later regions and hides dungeon listings there.

### Active
- Expand all region dimensions and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content; only Greendale has been updated so far.
- Remove Camp Provisioner and Field Smith from regions after Ironcrag while retaining quest keepers and Greendale-return teleporters.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Apply expanded dimensions and repositioned landmarks to every region in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes, landmarks, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, resource nodes, and enemy population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, return behavior, death respawn, and saved coordinates.
- `src/ui.js`: World-map travel UI, NPC services, and region progress display.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `src/game.js` and `src/ui.js` had pre-existing modifications, and `src/data.js` now includes the Greendale expansion. Preserve and inspect these changes.
- Region sizes were originally 34–38 tiles across eight regions in `REGION_ORDER`; Greendale is now size 56 with spawn `[28, 33]`, village `[28, 26]`, and lair `[46, 44]`.
- `buildWorld()` still adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, conflicting with the service-location requirement.
- Landmark coordinates, ponds, and village/lair layouts use fixed offsets; resource nodes remain at 8, normal enemies at 15, and roadside details at 18.
- Renderer pre-renders all ground tiles; minimap updates periodically. Both costs grow with map size.
- Saved region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`.
- No root `package.json` was found; no tests or runtime verification have been performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand all AETHERIA regions for more varied exploration while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Keep the game mobile-playable and optimized, with future multiplayer capacity and no fake players.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- From regions after Ironcrag, leyline travel is restricted to Greendale.
- Returning from later regions and dying there sends the player to Greendale.
- Greendale is being expanded to size 56, with spawn `[28, 33]`, village `[28, 26]`, and lair `[46, 44]`.
- Other region sizes have not yet been decided.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Game.travelTo()` blocks travel from regions after Ironcrag to destinations other than Greendale.
- `returnToHub()` and death respawn send players in later regions to Greendale.
- `panelMap()` shows only Greendale as the travel destination from later regions and hides dungeon listings there.
- Greendale’s dimensions and landmark coordinates have been expanded/repositioned in `src/data.js`.

### Active
- Expand the remaining regions and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content.
- Remove Camp Provisioner and Field Smith from regions after Ironcrag while retaining quest keepers and Greendale-return teleporters.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose expanded dimensions and reposition landmarks for all regions in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes, landmarks, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, resource nodes, and enemy population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, return behavior, death respawn, and saved coordinates.
- `src/ui.js`: World-map travel UI, NPC services, and region progress display.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `src/game.js` and `src/ui.js` had pre-existing modifications. Preserve and inspect these changes.
- Remaining regions are 34–38 tiles across; only Greendale is currently size 56.
- `buildWorld()` still adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, conflicting with the service-location requirement.
- Landmark coordinates, ponds, and village/lair layouts use fixed offsets; resource nodes remain at 8, normal enemies at 15, and roadside details at 18.
- Renderer pre-renders all ground tiles; minimap updates periodically. Both costs grow with map size.
- Saved region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`.
- No root `package.json` was found; no tests or runtime verification have been performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand all AETHERIA regions for more varied exploration while preserving gameplay and saved progress.
- Keep the game mobile-playable and optimized, with future multiplayer capacity and no fake players.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- From regions after Ironcrag, leyline travel is restricted to Greendale.
- Returning from later regions and dying there sends the player to Greendale.
- Greendale is size 56, with spawn `[28, 33]`, village `[28, 26]`, and lair `[46, 44]`.
- Remaining region sizes and landmark positions are still undecided.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Game.travelTo()` blocks travel from regions after Ironcrag to destinations other than Greendale.
- `returnToHub()` and death respawn send players in later regions to Greendale.
- `panelMap()` shows only Greendale as the travel destination from later regions and hides dungeon listings there.
- Greendale’s dimensions and landmark coordinates were expanded/repositioned in `src/data.js`.

### Active
- Expand the remaining regions and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content.
- Remove Camp Provisioner and Field Smith from regions after Ironcrag while retaining quest keepers and Greendale-return teleporters.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose expanded dimensions and reposition landmarks for all regions in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes, landmarks, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, resource nodes, and enemy population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, return behavior, death respawn, and saved coordinates.
- `src/ui.js`: World-map travel UI, NPC services, and region progress display.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `src/game.js` and `src/ui.js` had pre-existing modifications. Preserve and inspect these changes.
- Remaining regions are 34–38 tiles across; only Greendale is currently size 56.
- `buildWorld()` still adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, conflicting with the service-location requirement.
- Landmark coordinates, ponds, and village/lair layouts use fixed offsets; resource nodes remain at 8, normal enemies at 15, and roadside details at 18.
- Renderer pre-renders all ground tiles; minimap updates periodically. Both costs grow with map size.
- Saved region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`.
- No root `package.json` was found; no tests or runtime verification have been performed.

- Keep the game mobile-playable and optimized, with future multiplayer capacity and no fake players.

## Requirements
- Expand every region and provide more room to explore.
- Keep town services on Greendale and Ironcrag; later regions retain quest access and have only a teleporter returning to Greendale.
- Preserve graphics, characters, classes, quests, items, gameplay systems, and saved progress.
- Do not simulate fake online players; make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and state them at completion.

## Decisions
- From regions after Ironcrag, leyline travel is restricted to Greendale.
- Returning from later regions and dying there sends the player to Greendale.
- Greendale is size 56, with spawn `[28, 33]`, village `[28, 26]`, and lair `[46, 44]`.
- Remaining region sizes and landmark positions are still undecided.

## Work State
### Completed
- `Game.travelTo()` blocks travel from regions after Ironcrag to destinations other than Greendale.
- `returnToHub()` and death respawn send players in later regions to Greendale.
- `panelMap()` shows only Greendale as the travel destination from later regions and hides dungeon listings there.
- Greendale’s dimensions and landmark coordinates were expanded/repositioned in `src/data.js`.

### Active
- Expand the remaining regions and reposition landmarks, water, paths, and content.
- Remove Camp Provisioner and Field Smith from regions after Ironcrag while retaining quest keepers and Greendale-return teleporters.
- Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
- Test traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Choose expanded dimensions and reposition landmarks for all regions in `src/data.js`.
2. Adjust terrain generation, NPC placement, content density, and teleporter behavior in `src/world.js`, `src/game.js`, and `src/ui.js`.
3. Review renderer and minimap performance for larger worlds.
4. Test world traversal, transitions, teleporters, saved progress, and mobile performance.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data.js`: Region sizes, landmarks, NPC definitions, dungeons, and quests.
- `src/world.js`: Terrain generation, NPC placement, scenery, resource nodes, and enemy population.
- `src/game.js`: Region transitions, teleportation, return behavior, death respawn, and saved coordinates.
- `src/ui.js`: World-map travel UI, NPC services, and region progress display.
- `src/renderer.js`: Ground rendering, camera, entity rendering, and minimap.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `src/game.js` and `src/ui.js` had pre-existing modifications. Preserve and inspect these changes.
- Remaining regions are 34–38 tiles across; only Greendale is currently size 56.
- `buildWorld()` still adds a Camp Provisioner and Field Smith to every non-Greendale region, conflicting with the service-location requirement.
- Landmark coordinates, ponds, and village/lair layouts use fixed offsets; resource nodes remain at 8, normal enemies at 15, and roadside details at 18.
- Renderer pre-renders all ground tiles; minimap updates periodically. Both costs grow with map size.
- Saved region and coordinates persist in `state.char.region`, `state.char.x`, and `state.char.y`.
- No root `package.json` was found; no tests or runtime verification have been performed.
